svg.title: General notes. 1. Thrust is cheap. Controlled thrust is the whole job. Shipping a demo is thrust. Keeping it upright in production is trust. 2. I sit on both sides of the table. In the room with clients and executives for the readout, the scope and the sign-off; back in the code for the hard parts. Nothing is lost in translation, because there is no translation. 3. I own systems from the first drawing to the runbook. The architecture, the product, the safety layer, the release, and the team that builds it. The same hands write a Rust power API, a guarded SQL agent and a Terraform module. 4. Most of the work sits in the unglamorous middle. Orchestration, the schema that refuses bad data, the job queue that survives a restart. 5. Decisions are written down. Decision records, specs, runbooks and handoff notes ship with the code, so the next team starts where I stopped. 6. Numbers come with their conditions. When a figure appears in one of my READMEs, a results file sits behind it. 7. AI where it earns its place. When a saved answer or a plain rule will do, no model is called. Everything else fails loud.
svg.text: GENERAL NOTES · 7 NOTES · READ BEFORE THE DRAWINGS
